archetypes.name: cwd-callsite-audit
archetypes.rationale: The fix threads cwd=_consumer_repo_root() into only _run_post_apply; the plan's open question asks whether other _run_command call sites in the loop also need the consumer cwd, but this was left unaddressed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every _run_command call site in python/plan_review.py — specifically _run_continuation, _exec_pause_save, and the step3-state invocation — and determine whether any of them also need the consumer-repo cwd rather than _REPO_ROOT (the same wrong-cwd-in-loop class as #4509). Verify that _consumer_repo_root() being resolved inside _run_post_apply() at call time (rather than captured once at loop entry in run_step3_review) is safe across multiple loop iterations where the process cwd could theoretically change. Check that adding the cwd parameter to _run_command with a None → _REPO_ROOT fallback is backward-compatible for all existing callers that do not pass cwd. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: violation-counter-threading
archetypes.rationale: pre_scrub_violations accumulates across _copy_tree_redacted then is passed as a CLI arg to run-log commit where it is added to copy_tree_violations; the partial-failure bail path silently drops the partial count.
archetypes.prompt_body: In python/design_log_publish_flow.py, when _copy_tree_redacted returns (False, total) for a child failure, the caller _publish_design_logs immediately returns (False, '', '', '', '0') without propagating the accumulated pre_scrub_violations total — verify whether this silent drop is intentional and document any operator-visible consequence. In python/run_logs.py, _commit_run computes violations = pre_scrub_violations + copy_tree_violations and emits SECRET_SCRUB_VIOLATIONS; check whether the two scrub passes (_copy_tree_redacted in design_log_publish_flow.py and _scrub_run_tree in run_logs.py) operate on the same physical files and could double-count the same violation. Verify the isdigit() validation in larch_log_commit_main correctly rejects negative strings such as '-1'. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
